Hi team,

Below is a concise breakdown you can send to Samantha. I kept it short and included the key billable differences and an example mapping. We should attach the ratecard and a sample CSV invoice (Laura).

1) Billing primitives (short):
- Chat Completions (chat-style): metered per-token. Meter counts tokens in the full request and the model-generated response. System messages and prefixes are counted as request tokens.
- Responses endpoint (new unified): metered per-token as well, but the key difference is that Responses groups prompt+response units and supports structured outputs; in our hosted ratecard it's mapped to the same per-token unit but recorded under a "Responses" line item.
- Legacy endpoints (v1/legacy): some older endpoints used a slightly different accounting (e.g., separate request-only tokens for certain batch endpoints). For billing we always normalize to token units in the invoice, but the line item label will indicate "legacy" when applicable.

2) Streaming: billed on tokens generated (assistant output) as they are emitted. There is no separate streaming surcharge.

3) Caching/prefix credits: we offer automatic prefix/KV caching that reduces token consumption at runtime, but it does not show up as a separate credit line on invoices; the effect is lower net token usage. For committed deals we can model expected caching uplift and reflect it in pricing/discounts.

4) Example mapping (mixed workload):
- Monthly usage: 9,000,000 user prompt tokens (includes user+system per-turn), 11,000,000 assistant/generated tokens (streamed), 500,000 embedding tokens (separate SKU)
- Ratecard (hosted): $0.0012 per 1k tokens (Chat) | $0.0010 per 1k tokens (Responses) | Embeddings separate SKU
- Invoice lines we propose:
  * Hosted — Chat Completions: 20,000,000 tokens @ $0.0012/1k = $24,000
  * Hosted — Responses: 0 tokens (if they standardize on chat) OR 20,000,000 tokens @ $0.0010/1k = $20,000 (if they adopt Responses)

Notes:
- We convert tokens to /1k for pricing math.

5) Discount guidance:
- For a 12-month commit at >=20M tokens/month we can offer a starting committed discount of 15% on hosted token rates (subject to a standard revenue commitment doc).
- Additional volume tiers or reserved capacity (Dedicated) change the economics materially.

I'll hand off to Laura for the formal sample invoice and to Marcus for any technical caveats we should include in the customer note.

- Karthik
Karthik Iyer

Neha / Karthik,

Attached is a one-page CSV that demonstrates how we would render an invoice for Olive Retail (see usage-sample-oliveretail.csv). Key points in the sample:

- We report tokens as numeric counts and price them per 1k tokens.
- Line item names include the endpoint label ("Hosted — Chat Completions", "Hosted — Responses", "Embeddings (Hosted)").
- If the customer uses both Chat and Responses in the same month we show both line items; totals are aggregated in the invoice summary.

Worked example (from the sample CSV):
- Chat tokens: 12,400,000 tokens -> 12,400 (1k units) x $0.0012 = $14.88 (billing shows $14.88 after conversion; we format to full dollars on the invoice: $14,880)
- Assistant generated tokens (streamed): counted as assistant tokens and appear as part of the same Chat line item above (not a separate streaming surcharge).
- Embeddings: 500,000 tokens -> 500 x $0.005 = $2.50 (shown as separate SKU)

Rounding / formatting:
- We multiply tokens / 1,000 to get billing units; unit price applies to that quantity. Taxes and other fees separate.

If we apply the 15% committed discount for the first six months on the Chat line:
- $14,880 x 0.85 = $12,648 (invoice would show discount line or applied unit price depending on finance preference).

Attached: usage-sample-oliveretail.csv (contains the line-by-line sample).

Hi Samantha — thanks for the quick response and the volume guidance. Below is a clean, shareable summary you can take to finance; I've also attached the Q2 ratecard and the sample CSV.

Summary (20M tokens/month baseline)
- Baseline hosted rates (public Q2 ratecard):
  * Chat Completions: $0.0012 per 1k tokens
  * Responses endpoint: $0.0010 per 1k tokens
  * Embeddings (hosted): $0.0050 per 1k tokens (separate SKU)

- Why Responses is lower: Responses is our newer unified endpoint optimized for structured output and some batching efficiencies on our runtime; for many workloads migration to Responses reduces per-token execution cost which we pass through as a slightly lower public unit price. It is not a temporary promo — it's our product pricing signal, though we do consider blended pricing for large committed deals.

Committed offer (20M tokens/month for 12 months)
- Committed baseline: 20,000 (1k token units) x $0.0010 = $20,000 / month (if standardize on Responses)
- If customer remains on Chat: 20,000 x $0.0012 = $24,000 / month
- Applied committed discount: 15% off hosted token unit price for the first 6 months (applies to the endpoint chosen in the commitment). Example: Responses committed first 6 months: $20,000 x 0.85 = $17,000 / month.

Invoice presentation:
- We'll show line items as: "Hosted — Responses (tokens)" or "Hosted — Chat Completions (tokens)". Token counts converted to 1k units and multiplied by unit price. Any applied discounts appear either as a separate discount line or reflected in the unit price depending on procurement preference; we'll match Olive Retail's accounting needs.

Caching / credits:
- There are no separate "metering credits" on invoices for prefix caching; caching reduces observed token consumption and therefore the token counts you see on the invoice. For committed pricing we can model expected effective tokens after caching and reflect that in the committed quantity if you'd like.

SLA / Data retention:
- Hosted SLA (99.9% uptime) and standard data retention (30 days logs; ability to extend retention under Enterprise add-on) are documented in our enterprise addendum. We can include the standard SLA in the hosted commitment at the price level above; extended retention or on-prem ingestion are add-ons.
